name: Mapungubwe Decline Conflicts
description: Late-thirteenth-century abandonment of the Mapungubwe capital associated with regional climate shock and rising rival Great Zimbabwe; no named battles survive but the polity's collapse is treated as a contested transition by Huffman.

name: Torwa-Changamire War
description: Changamire Dombo's overthrow of the Torwa dynasty at Khami and the founding of the Rozvi Empire on the southwestern Zimbabwe Plateau.

name: Portuguese-Mutapa War (1568-1575)
description: Francisco Barreto's failed Portuguese expedition up the Zambezi to seize the gold mines of Mutapa, recounted by Beach and Newitt as the opening Portuguese intervention.

name: Battle of Massapa
description: Engagement during the Barreto expedition against the Mongas, fought near the Portuguese feira of Massapa on the Mutapa frontier.

name: Mutapa Civil War (1628-1629)
description: Capture and overthrow of Mavura Mhande as Portuguese-backed claimants seized the Mutapa throne, effectively reducing Mutapa to a Portuguese vassal.

name: Mutapa Revolt of 1693
description: Changamire Dombo's destruction of the Portuguese trading fairs at Dambarare and his expulsion of Portuguese settlers from the Zimbabwe plateau.

name: Battle of Maungwe
description: Dombo's defeat of a Portuguese force in Manyika, prefiguring the 1693 expulsion.

name: Maravi Confederacy Wars
description: Expansion of the Maravi/Kalonga paramountcy and the Lundu raids led by Muzura into Portuguese Zambezia, described in Newitt's history of Mozambique.

name: Zimba Raids
description: Northward sweep of the Zimba war-bands from the Lower Zambezi up the Swahili coast, sacking Kilwa and besieging Mombasa.

name: Khoikhoi-Dutch Wars
description: First (1659-60) and Second (1673-77) Khoekhoe-Dutch Wars at the Cape, the earliest sustained armed resistance to Dutch settlement.

name: First Khoikhoi-Dutch War
description: Cattle-raiding war led by Doman against the early VOC settlement at the Cape.

name: Second Khoikhoi-Dutch War
description: VOC commando campaigns against the Cochoqua paramount Gonnema, ending in Khoekhoe submission.

name: Sakalava-Merina Wars
description: Imerina's campaigns under Radama I and Ranavalona I to subdue the Sakalava kingdoms of western Madagascar.

name: Merina Unification Wars
description: Andrianampoinimerina's unification of the four Merina kingdoms and expansion across the central highlands, the foundation of Imerina state-building Larson analyses.

name: Radama I's Conquests
description: Radama I's British-armed campaigns extending Merina rule over most of Madagascar.

name: First Franco-Hova War
description: French naval bombardment and occupation of Tamatave forcing the 1885 protectorate treaty over Madagascar.

name: Second Franco-Hova War
description: French expeditionary conquest of Madagascar ending the Merina monarchy and annexing the island.

name: Menalamba Rebellion
description: Anti-French and anti-Christian uprising in Imerina suppressed by Gallieni's pacification campaign.

name: First Cape Frontier War
description: Opening Boer-Xhosa frontier war over cattle and grazing along the Great Fish River.

name: Second Cape Frontier War
description: Second Xhosa-Boer frontier war involving Ndlambe and Rharhabe Xhosa against trekboer commandos.

name: Third Cape Frontier War
description: Joint Xhosa-Khoekhoe rising during the first British occupation of the Cape, the largest pre-1811 frontier war.

name: Fourth Cape Frontier War
description: Colonel Graham's expulsion of Ndlambe Xhosa across the Fish River and founding of Grahamstown.

name: Fifth Cape Frontier War
description: Makhanda's attack on Grahamstown and the British counter-offensive that drove Xhosa east of the Keiskamma.

name: Battle of Grahamstown
description: Makhanda Nxele's 22 April 1819 assault on the British garrison at Grahamstown, repulsed with heavy Xhosa losses.

name: Sixth Cape Frontier War
description: Large Xhosa invasion of the Cape Colony triggering D'Urban's annexation of the Queen Adelaide Province and a major Voortrekker precipitant.

name: War of the Axe
description: Seventh Cape Frontier War, also known as the War of the Axe, ending in British annexation of British Kaffraria.

name: Eighth Cape Frontier War
description: Mlanjeni's War, the longest and bloodiest of the Cape Frontier Wars, featuring the Waterkloof guerrilla campaign and Kat River rebellion.

name: Ninth Cape Frontier War
description: Final Cape Frontier War ending Xhosa political independence on the Transkei frontier.

name: Xhosa Cattle-Killing Movement
description: Millenarian prophecy of Nongqawuse triggering mass cattle slaughter and the collapse of independent Xhosa power, treated as a 'silent war' in Cape Frontier historiography.

name: Battle of Gqokli Hill
description: Shaka's defensive victory over Zwide's Ndwandwe army, a hinge engagement of the Mfecane.

name: Battle of Mhlatuze River
description: Decisive Zulu rout of the Ndwandwe that broke Zwide's confederation and sent Soshangane, Zwangendaba and Nxaba into the diaspora.

name: Mzilikazi's Migration
description: Mzilikazi's flight from Shaka and the violent path of Ndebele state-formation across the Highveld into Matabeleland.

name: Kololo Migration
description: Sebetwane's Kololo trek from the Highveld to the upper Zambezi and conquest of the Lozi/Bulozi kingdom.

name: Ngoni Migrations
description: Northward migrations of Zwangendaba and Maseko Ngoni from Zululand across the Zambezi into Malawi and southern Tanzania.

name: Gaza Empire Wars
description: Soshangane's founding of the Gaza Empire and the long series of expansion and succession wars culminating in Portuguese conquest of Gungunhana.

name: Soshangane-Zwangendaba War
description: Clash between the two Mfecane diaspora paramounts pushing Zwangendaba's Ngoni north of the Zambezi.

name: Battle of Vegkop
description: Voortrekker laager defeat of a large Matabele force, the first major engagement of the Great Trek.

name: Battle of Mosega
description: Voortrekker dawn raid on Mzilikazi's Marico settlements, opening the campaign that drove the Ndebele to Matabeleland.

name: Battle of Kapain
description: Nine-day Voortrekker pursuit of Mzilikazi that forced the Ndebele to abandon the Highveld for the Limpopo.

name: Battle of Italeni
description: Voortrekker defeat by Dingane's impis on the way to avenge Piet Retief.

name: Weenen Massacre
description: Dingane's Zulu attacks on Voortrekker laagers along the Bushman's River following the killing of Piet Retief.

name: Battle of Maritz River (Veglaer)
description: Successful Voortrekker defence of the Veglaer laager against a Zulu impi in August 1838.

name: Zulu Civil War of 1840
description: Mpande's revolt against Dingane, fought at Maqongqo with Voortrekker support, ending Dingane's reign.

name: Battle of Congella
description: Voortrekker ambush of British forces at Port Natal, leading to the siege relieved by Dick King's ride.

name: Battle of Boomplaats
description: Harry Smith's defeat of Andries Pretorius cementing the short-lived Orange River Sovereignty.

name: Basotho Gun War
description: Basotho rejection of Cape disarmament that forced the transfer of Basutoland back to direct imperial control.

name: Free State-Basotho War (Senekal's War)
description: First Free State-Basotho War over the Caledon River frontier, ending in the Treaty of Aliwal North.

name: Seqiti Wars
description: Second and Third Free State-Basotho wars (Seqiti) culminating in Moshoeshoe's appeal for British protection and the founding of Basutoland.

name: Siege of Thaba Bosiu
description: Moshoeshoe I's defence of his mountain capital against repeated Free State assaults.

name: Battle of Berea
description: Sir George Cathcart's defeat by Moshoeshoe I above the Caledon River.

name: Hlubi War
description: Langalibalele rebellion of the Hlubi chiefdom in Natal and the Bushman's River Pass engagement.

name: Sekhukhune Wars
description: Successive Boer and British campaigns culminating in Wolseley's 1879 storming of Tsate that broke Pedi independence.

name: Battle of Tsate
description: Wolseley's November 1879 storming of Sekhukhune's mountain stronghold ending the Pedi War.

name: Battle of Isandlwana
description: Catastrophic British defeat by Cetshwayo's Zulu army on 22 January 1879.

name: Battle of Rorke's Drift
description: Defence of the mission station by Chard and Bromhead's company on 22-23 January 1879.

name: Battle of Nyezane
description: Colonel Pearson's coastal column victory over the Zulu on the same day as Isandlwana.

name: Siege of Eshowe
description: Investment of Pearson's coastal column in the Norwegian mission at Eshowe.

name: Battle of Hlobane
description: Buller's failed mounted raid on the Hlobane plateau, the worst British reverse of the war after Isandlwana.

name: Battle of Khambula
description: Wood's defensive victory the day after Hlobane, considered by many the turning point of the Anglo-Zulu War.

name: Battle of Gingindlovu
description: Chelmsford's relief column victory en route to Eshowe.

name: Battle of Ulundi
description: Decisive British victory on 4 July 1879 destroying the Zulu royal kraal and ending the war.

name: Battle of Intombe
description: Zulu raid on a British supply convoy on the Intombe River in March 1879.

name: Anglo-Zulu Civil War (uSuthu vs Mandlakazi)
description: Cetshwayo's restoration war and the subsequent uSuthu-Mandlakazi conflict ending in British annexation of Zululand.

name: Battle of Majuba Hill
description: Decisive Boer victory ending the First Anglo-Boer War.

name: Battle of Laing's Nek
description: First major engagement of the First Boer War, a Boer defensive victory on the Drakensberg pass.

name: Battle of Ingogo
description: Boer attack on Colley's column at Schuinshoogte/Ingogo during the First Boer War.

name: Jameson Raid
description: Leander Starr Jameson's abortive raid into the Transvaal that helped precipitate the Second Anglo-Boer War.

name: Siege of Mafeking
description: Baden-Powell's 217-day defence of Mafeking, the most famous siege of the Second Boer War.

name: Siege of Ladysmith
description: 118-day Boer investment of White's army in Ladysmith, relieved by Buller in February 1900.

name: Siege of Kimberley
description: Four-month Boer siege of the diamond town with Cecil Rhodes inside, relieved by French's cavalry.

name: Battle of Stormberg
description: First Black Week defeat: Gatacre's column routed by Olivier in the northern Cape.

name: Battle of Magersfontein
description: Cronjé and De la Rey's defeat of Methuen's Kimberley relief column, the second Black Week disaster.

name: Battle of Colenso
description: Buller's defeat on the Tugela attempting to relieve Ladysmith, completing Black Week.

name: Battle of Spion Kop
description: Botha's defeat of Warren's attempt to outflank the Tugela line, a fixture of First World War tactical literature.

name: Battle of Vaal Krantz
description: Third failed Buller attempt to break through to Ladysmith.

name: Battle of Tugela Heights
description: Buller's fourth and successful breakthrough of the Tugela line relieving Ladysmith.

name: Battle of Paardeberg
description: Roberts's encirclement and surrender of Cronjé's army, the turning point of the conventional phase.

name: Battle of Diamond Hill
description: Roberts's June 1900 engagement east of Pretoria, the last large conventional battle of the war.

name: Battle of Bergendal
description: Final set-piece engagement of the Second Boer War's conventional phase, in the eastern Transvaal.

name: Battle of Sannaspos
description: De Wet's ambush of Broadwood's column at the Bloemfontein waterworks, a hallmark of the guerrilla phase.

name: Battle of Bothaville
description: British surprise dawn attack on De Wet's laager, the largest single Free State commando loss.

name: Battle of Tweebosch
description: De la Rey's capture of Lord Methuen, the most famous Boer victory of the guerrilla phase.

name: First Matabele War
description: BSAC conquest of Lobengula's Ndebele Kingdom and seizure of Bulawayo.

name: Shangani Patrol
description: Annihilation of Allan Wilson's BSAC patrol pursuing Lobengula, the Rhodesian Custer myth.

name: Battle of Bembesi
description: Maxim-gun rout of Lobengula's regiments opening the way to Bulawayo.

name: Second Matabele War
description: First Chimurenga: Ndebele-Shona uprising against BSAC rule and Rhodes's Matobo Hills indaba.

name: Gungunhana War
description: Portuguese campaign against Ngungunyane culminating in the battles of Marracuene, Magul and Coolela and his capture at Chaimite.

name: Battle of Marracuene
description: Mouzinho de Albuquerque's defeat of the Gaza impis north of Lourenço Marques.

name: Battle of Coolela
description: Decisive Portuguese victory over Ngungunyane's army, leading to the storming of Chaimite.

name: Barue Rebellion
description: Large anti-Portuguese uprising in central Mozambique during World War I, suppressed with Nguni and Ngoni levies.

name: Bambatha Rebellion
description: Poll-tax rebellion led by Chief Bambatha kaMancinza, the last major armed Zulu resistance to colonial rule.

name: Mphezeni's War
description: BSAC campaign breaking the Ngoni paramountcy of Mpezeni in eastern Zambia.

name: Yao Wars
description: Series of British campaigns against Yao slave-trading chiefdoms Mlozi, Makanjira, Zarafi and Kawinga in modern Malawi.

name: Karonga War
description: African Lakes Company campaign against Mlozi bin Kazbadema's slaving stockades at the north end of Lake Malawi.

name: Lozi-Makololo War
description: Lozi restoration war that overthrew the Kololo conquerors and reinstated the Lewanika line.

name: Chilembwe Uprising
description: John Chilembwe's January 1915 rising in Nyasaland against colonial labour conditions and the war effort.

name: Herero War
description: Samuel Maharero's rising and the German Schutztruppe campaign culminating in the Battle of Waterberg and the Omaheke extermination order.

name: Battle of Waterberg
description: Trotha's encirclement of Maharero's Herero camp on 11 August 1904, the prelude to the Omaheke genocide.

name: Nama War
description: Hendrik Witbooi's and Jakob Morenga's guerrilla war against the German Schutztruppe in southern Namibia.

name: Bondelswarts Rebellion (1903)
description: Earlier Bondelswarts revolt that diverted German troops from Hereroland and helped trigger the 1904 Herero rising.

name: Bondelswarts Rebellion (1922)
description: South African aerial bombardment of Abraham Morris's Bondelswarts community, an early test of the League of Nations Mandate.

name: Maharero's War
description: Long pre-colonial Herero-Nama conflict between Maharero and Hendrik Witbooi over cattle and the central highlands.

name: Khauas Hottentot Uprising
description: Leutwein's campaign breaking the Khauas under Andries Lambert and forcing Witbooi's submission at Naukluft.

name: Battle of Naukluft
description: Leutwein's mountain campaign forcing Hendrik Witbooi to accept German protection.

name: Mandume's War
description: Portuguese and South African campaigns against Mandume ya Ndemufayo's Kwanyama kingdom in Ovamboland.

name: Battle of Mufilo
description: Portuguese defeat of the Kwanyama at Mongua/Mufilo driving Mandume south of the Cunene.

name: South West Africa Campaign
description: South African conquest of German South West Africa in WWI, including the battles of Sandfontein and Trekkopjes.

name: Maritz Rebellion
description: Boer uprising led by Maritz, De Wet and Beyers against Botha's decision to invade German South West Africa.

name: East Africa Campaign (Northern Rhodesia and Nyasaland front)
description: Lettow-Vorbeck's incursions into Nyasaland and Northern Rhodesia, including the surrender at Abercorn after the Armistice.

name: Rand Rebellion
description: Armed white-miner uprising on the Witwatersrand crushed by Smuts with artillery and aircraft.

name: Mozambican War of Independence
description: FRELIMO's ten-year guerrilla war against Portuguese rule, central to Newitt and Henriksen's accounts.

name: Operation Gordian Knot
description: General Kaúlza de Arriaga's massive 1970 counter-insurgency sweep in Cabo Delgado and Niassa.

name: Wiriyamu Massacre
description: Portuguese commando massacre exposed by Adrian Hastings, a hinge event in the discrediting of Lisbon's African wars.

name: Sharpeville Massacre
description: Police killing of 69 anti-pass demonstrators that triggered the banning of the ANC/PAC and the armed struggle.

name: Soweto Uprising
description: Township uprising sparked by the Afrikaans-medium decree, opening a decade of mass unrest.

name: Township Wars (KwaZulu-Natal Conflict)
description: Inkatha-ANC violence in Natal and on the Reef during the late-apartheid transition.

name: Battle of Cuito Cuanavale
description: Largest land battle in Africa since WWII, the culmination of the South African Border War.

name: Operation Savannah
description: First major SADF incursion into Angola in support of UNITA and FNLA.

name: Battle of Cassinga
description: SADF airborne raid on the SWAPO camp at Cassinga, a touchstone event of the Border War.

name: Operation Reindeer
description: Combined SADF airborne and mechanised strikes against SWAPO bases including Cassinga.

name: Operation Protea
description: Largest SADF mechanised operation in southern Angola, capturing Xangongo and Ongiva.

name: Operation Askari
description: SADF dry-season offensive into Cunene province ending in the Lusaka Accord.

name: Operation Modular
description: SADF/UNITA blocking of FAPLA's offensive on the Lomba, the opening phase of Cuito Cuanavale.

name: Operation Hooper
description: SADF attempt to push FAPLA west of the Cuito River into the Tumpo Triangle.

name: Operation Packer
description: Final SADF set-piece attacks on the Tumpo Triangle before disengagement.

name: Mozambican Civil War
description: FRELIMO-RENAMO civil war ending in the Rome General Peace Accords.

name: Gorongosa Campaign
description: FRELIMO/Zimbabwean ZNA storming of the RENAMO headquarters at Casa Banana.

name: Renamo Insurgency (2013-2021)
description: Low-intensity RENAMO armed resurgence in central Mozambique ending in the 2019 peace deal and 2021 demobilisation.

name: Cabo Delgado Insurgency
description: Ansar al-Sunna / ISCAP jihadist insurgency in northern Mozambique drawing SADC and Rwandan intervention.

name: Battle of Palma
description: ISCAP raid on the LNG town of Palma that triggered the SADC/Rwandan intervention.

name: Lesotho Coups and Civil Conflict
description: Successive coups and mutinies including 1970, 1986, 1991 and the 1998 crisis.

name: Operation Boleas
description: 1998 SADC (South Africa/Botswana) military intervention to suppress the Lesotho army mutiny.

name: 1986 Lesotho Coup
description: South African-backed Lekhanya coup ousting Leabua Jonathan.

name: Madagascar 1947 Uprising
description: Anti-colonial revolt and bloody French suppression, the largest African colonial war between 1945 and Algeria.

name: 1972 Madagascar Rotaka
description: Student/worker uprising that toppled Tsiranana and ended the First Republic.

name: 2009 Madagascar Political Crisis
description: Rajoelina's army-backed overthrow of Marc Ravalomanana.

name: Comoros Coups (Bob Denard era)
description: Series of mercenary coups under Bob Denard ending with Operation Azalee in 1995.

name: Operation Azalee
description: French intervention ending Denard's 1995 coup against President Djohar.

name: Anjouan Crisis
description: Anjouan secession, repeated coups and the 2008 AU/Comoran 'Operation Democracy in Comoros' that ended Mohamed Bacar's regime.

name: Operation Democracy in Comoros
description: AU-backed Comoran invasion of Anjouan ending the Bacar separatist regime.

name: Seychelles 1981 Mercenary Raid
description: Mike Hoare's 'Frothblowers' attempted coup against René, ending in a hijacking back to South Africa.

name: Operation Vula
description: ANC clandestine return programme that infiltrated MK cadres back into South Africa.

name: Church Street Bombing
description: MK car bombing outside SAAF headquarters, the largest urban bombing of the apartheid era.

name: Bisho Massacre
description: Ciskei Defence Force shooting of ANC marchers, a flashpoint of the South African transition.

name: Boipatong Massacre
description: Inkatha hostel-dweller massacre that derailed CODESA negotiations.

name: Bophuthatswana Crisis
description: March 1994 collapse of the Bophuthatswana homeland and AWB incursion that paved the way for the first democratic elections.

name: Marikana Massacre
description: Police killing of 34 striking platinum miners, the deadliest state violence in democratic South Africa.

name: 2021 South African Unrest
description: Looting and riots in KwaZulu-Natal and Gauteng triggered by Jacob Zuma's imprisonment.

name: Caprivi Conflict
description: Brief separatist uprising in the Caprivi Strip by the CLA, suppressed by Namibian forces.

name: Operation Dingo
description: Rhodesian airborne raid on ZANLA bases at Chimoio and Tembue in Mozambique.

name: Battle of Sinoia
description: Skirmish conventionally treated as the opening engagement of the Second Chimurenga / Rhodesian Bush War.

name: Nyadzonia Raid
description: Selous Scouts raid on the ZANLA refugee camp at Nyadzonia/Pungwe.

name: Westgate Strike (Operation Eland)
description: Selous Scouts cross-border raid on the ZANLA Nyadzonia camp.

name: Gukurahundi
description: Mugabe's Fifth Brigade campaign in Matabeleland and the Midlands targeting ZAPU supporters.

name: Zimbabwe Farm Invasions
description: ZANU-PF-backed seizures of white-owned farms accompanied by political violence.

name: South African Raid on Maseru
description: SADF cross-border raid on suspected ANC houses in Maseru, December 1982.

name: South African Raid on Matola
description: SADF special-forces raid on ANC houses in the Maputo suburb of Matola.

name: Battle of Bangui (2013)
description: South African SANDF battalion's stand against Séléka rebels in Bangui, the largest SANDF combat since 1994; included here for the South African dimension.

name: eSwatini 2021 Protests
description: Pro-democracy protests met with army deployment and dozens of deaths.
